title: Morning Notes in Blue
summary: A short entry about cool light, quiet rooms, and the way blue tones slow down attention.
main_text:
The room was still waking up when I entered, with the kind of light that makes every surface seem slightly cooler than it really is. A series of blue-heavy works lined the wall, and together they changed my breathing more than my thoughts. I found myself lingering longer, not because the paintings were difficult, but because they refused to hurry.

Blue can flatten a space or deepen it, depending on how bravely it is used. Here it did both. Some canvases felt open like early sky, while others held their color close, almost bruised, almost private. That tension gave the room its quiet pull.

I wrote these notes before leaving because the effect was easy to miss in conversation. Nothing dramatic happened. I simply walked in carrying the speed of the morning and walked out with less of it.
